question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to create shared global MCP declarations from manifests, and if so what host authorization, command-broker, environment, and role-scope contract governs them?
rationale: The branch makes a durable security and ownership-policy choice that cannot be safely inferred from a mechanical implementation preference; an exact configuration digest is not itself authorization to execute or share a local command.

options.title: Require host-authorized MCP resources
options.body: Adopt a brokered or allowlisted command path and explicit host-approved sharing scope before this lifecycle capability can merge.

options.title: Accept global shared ownership
options.body: Document and intentionally accept that a Claw may create or reuse a global MCP declaration, with the resulting cross-role execution and collision semantics.

options.title: Pause MCP lifecycle support
options.body: Keep MCP declarations outside the experimental Claw lifecycle until the authorization model is approved.

recommendation.title: Require host-authorized MCP resources
recommendation.body: Adopt a brokered or allowlisted command path and explicit host-approved sharing scope before this lifecycle capability can merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The assignment and earlier review findings connect this person most directly to the unresolved MCP lifecycle and source-config boundary.
